answer: Sybil resistance prices identity directly. A new agent posts a unit bond before its output is attestable; a yarrow sampler re-estimates that bond each epoch from the median honest payout times live identity count, so marginal cost grows at least linearly with n. The bond is protocol-enforced (unbonded output is discarded) and bound to a key a slash burns, so a farmer cannot reset or split it across puppets; each fake sparrow pays a full bond, no batch discount, while an honest agent pays once and recovers it after one clean epoch. That persistent gap is the canyon rule.
